<div class="article-top"><a class="back-link" href="../writing.html">← Writing</a><p class="eyebrow">Working paper / Project note</p><h1>Talent, Defined</h1><p class="page-deck">ByteDance and the changing meaning of good talent</p></div>

::: {.article-copy}

What counts as “good talent” when organizations imagine their future around AI?

Using ByteDance as a case, this study traces how descriptions of the valuable employee change alongside organizational priorities and expectations of technology. It asks how these descriptions become criteria for selection, assessment, and reward.

The study combines a historical reading of organizational discourse with questions about measurement: when the definition of talent changes, what happens to the meaning and comparability of an evaluation? The source corpus distinguishes first-party statements from reported accounts.

This work forms one strand of my wider research on [talent, valuation, and AI recruitment](../research/ai-talent.html).

:::
